overview: White prepares d4 without first developing the knight, a Ponziani-like idea that avoids Black's pins and the Scotch. Black normally answers 2...Nf6 3.d4 or 2...d5 and gets a comfortable game with equal chances. Quick tries such as the Lasa Gambit 2...f5 or the Norwalde 2...d5 3.Qh5 are rarer and I am less sure of them.

white_ideas.idea: Play d4 with a pawn centre on c3 and d4.
Develop Nf3, Bc4 and O-O, using c3 to support the centre.

black_ideas.idea: Meet it with ...Nf6 or ...d5 and attack the e4 pawn.
Use the extra tempo to equalise and exchange in the centre.

typical_structures.structure: Open game with c3/d4 against e5, resembling the Ponziani or Scotch.

character.notes: Quiet main line; no forcing play.

gambit.notes: No material in the main line; Lasa and Norwalde gambits are rare tries.

structure.notes: Centre in tension after d4, opening on exchange.

approach.notes: Rare at the top, chosen mainly for surprise.

sublines_that_differ.name: Norwalde Gambit
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. c3 d5 3. Qh5 Bd6

character.reason: Quiet equal main line, not especially solid.

structure.reason: Centre in tension, not yet decided.
